title: Password Management and Recovery
description: Implement password reset, change password, and account recovery features.

data.text: Password management is critical for user security. ASP.NET Core Identity provides built-in features for password reset, change password, and account recovery.
The password reset flow involves generating a token, sending it via email, and allowing the user to set a new password.

data.title: Password Reset Token Generation
data.content: Generate and send password reset token.

data.title: Password Reset Handler
data.content: Handle password reset with token validation.

data.text: Authenticated users can change their password without requiring a reset token. This is a common security feature.

data.title: Change Password Implementation
data.content: Allow users to change their password.

data.text: Identity automatically locks accounts after too many failed login attempts. This prevents brute force attacks.

data.title: Security Best Practices
data.text: Always use HTTPS for password-related operations. Password reset tokens should expire quickly (typically 1-24 hours). Never log passwords or reset tokens.
Configure password requirements to enforce strong passwords across your application.

data.title: Strong Password Policy

terms.definition: A security token generated by Identity that allows a user to reset their password without being logged in.
A security feature that temporarily disables an account after multiple failed login attempts.
Rules that define what constitutes a valid password, such as length, complexity, and character requirements.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Password reset uses tokens sent via email
Account lockout prevents brute force attacks
Always use HTTPS for password operations
data.takeaway: Password management features are essential for user security and account recovery.
